copy.text: First the plain carrier, then a short silence, then this bend. Both notes use the same loudness envelope.
Each press plays one 0.8-second note. Changing a control stops it; changing a control never plays it. Start with your volume low.
These are separate notes, not a mixture. The bending sine changes an angle in the resulting sound.
Hold the index shown here for one 0.8-second note. The evolving bend and kept comparison stay unchanged.

A falling bend reaches zero index after 0.60 seconds; a rising bend reaches the chosen index then. This plot freezes that instant; the heard note changes continuously. The amplitude envelope is unchanged.
The dashed line is the plain carrier on the same scale. At zero index, the resulting wave lies on it.
The mark shows one full repeat of this frozen shape. During a falling bend, the heard note keeps changing instead.
The gold dots mark the same instant in the source and result. Moving them is silent; it does not change either wave.
Two 0.8-second notes with 0.25 seconds of silence between. Each keeps the same amplitude envelope. Stop ends the whole comparison.
The orange wave keeps its own ratio, index, bend mode and inspected instant. Hearing it does not change the cyan wave. Return changes the controls only; it does not play a note.
The dashed orange line keeps its own frozen instant. Both shapes use the same four carrier cycles; showing it does not play either note.

cases.title: Bend a sine — Separate direct notes from two-note comparisons
cases.goal: Four direct notes and Stop remain easy to find. Comparing two notes is a separate deliberate choice, with its timing explanation beside it.
cases.steps: Inside #bend-live-sound after the direct-note/Stop action row add closed details #bend-comparisons. Move #bend-compare-plain and #bend-compare-frozen into it, with #bend-compare-plain-help and #bend-frozen-pair-help verbatim. The plain-pair paragraph currently resides in702 #bend-sound-guide; this card deliberately moves only that paragraph out to its comparison buttons. Keep other702 explanations in their guide, which remains a sibling of comparisons. Keep bend-listen, bend-listen-frozen, bend-listen-carrier, bend-listen-modulator, bend-stop, bend-sound-status, bend-sound-help and bend-frozen-help outside comparisons and visible. Preserve memory comparisons in #bend-memory; this card concerns only current-vs-plain/frozen pairs. No audio buffer/helper/pending-token change.
cases.message: direct sine notes and Stop stay visible while two-note comparisons keep their own timing explanation
